title: 2 Samuel 16: Ziba, Shimei's Cursing, and Absalom Defiles the Concubines
body:
Read the chapter → [2 Samuel 16](/bible/2-samuel/16)

## Introduction

Chapter 16 continues David's flight. Ziba meets him with provisions and slanders his master Mephibosheth to gain his inheritance, and Shimei of the house of Saul comes out cursing David and casting stones, blaming him for the blood of Saul's house. David refuses to let Abishai kill Shimei, submitting to the possibility that the Most High had bidden him curse, and trusting the Most High to requite him good. Meanwhile Hushai reaches Absalom in Jerusalem, and Ahithophel counsels Absalom to go in unto his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel, which fulfills the exact word the Most High spoke in chapter 12. None of this was coincidence; it was prophesied to happen because of what David did, and you cannot make this stuff up.

**[2 Samuel 16:1-4](/bible/2-samuel/16#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/2-samuel/16#v1)</sup> And when David was a little past the top of the hill, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him, with a couple of asses saddled, and upon them two hundred loaves of bread, and an hundred bunches of raisins, and an hundred of summer fruits, and a bottle of wine.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/2-samuel/16#v2)</sup> And the king said unto Ziba, What meanest thou by these? And Ziba said, The asses be for the king’s household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the wine, that such as be faint in the wilderness may drink.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/2-samuel/16#v3)</sup> And the king said, And where is thy master’s son? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he abideth at Jerusalem: for he said, To day shall the house of Israel restore me the kingdom of my father.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/2-samuel/16#v4)</sup> Then said the king to Ziba, Behold, thine are all that pertained unto Mephibosheth. And Ziba said, I humbly beseech thee that I may find grace in thy sight, my lord, O king.

- When David was past the top of the hill, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him with saddled asses, two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred bunches of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a bottle of wine. When David asked where his master's son was, Ziba said Mephibosheth abode in Jerusalem, saying the house of Israel would restore him the kingdom of his father. So David gave Ziba all that pertained to Mephibosheth.
- Ziba came with gifts, and when David asked about Mephibosheth, Ziba claimed Mephibosheth thought the kingdom was about to be restored to him, which was not true. On that word David handed Ziba everything that belonged to Mephibosheth.

**[2 Samuel 16:5-8](/bible/2-samuel/16#v5)**

> <sup>[5](/bible/2-samuel/16#v5)</sup> And when king David came to Bahurim, behold, thence came out a man of the family of the house of Saul, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera: he came forth, and cursed still as he came.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/2-samuel/16#v6)</sup> And he cast stones at David, and at all the servants of king David: and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/2-samuel/16#v7)</sup> And thus said Shimei when he cursed, Come out, come out, thou bloody man, and thou man of Belial:
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/2-samuel/16#v8)</sup> The Lord hath returned upon thee all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose stead thou hast reigned; and the Lord hath delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom thy son: and, behold, thou art taken in thy mischief, because thou art a bloody man.

- As David came to Bahurim, a man of the house of Saul named Shimei the son of Gera came out, cursing and casting stones at David and all his servants. Shimei cursed, calling David a bloody man and a man of Belial, saying the Most High had returned upon him all the blood of the house of Saul, and delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom his son, and taken him in his mischief because he was a bloody man.
- Shimei was of the house of Saul, and Saul was the wicked one who tried to kill David; it was by the hand of the Most High that Saul did not succeed. Yet Shimei cursed David as if David were in the wrong, because word gets around, people gossip and blame, and he saw David at a low state and went to rub it in his face. That is the mindset of some people in Israel as well.

**[2 Samuel 16:9-10](/bible/2-samuel/16#v9)**

> <sup>[9](/bible/2-samuel/16#v9)</sup> Then said Abishai the son of Zeruiah unto the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over, I pray thee, and take off his head.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/2-samuel/16#v10)</sup> And the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? so let him curse, because the Lord hath said unto him, Curse David. Who shall then say, Wherefore hast thou done so?

- Abishai the son of Zeruiah asked why this dead dog should curse the king, and offered to go take off his head. But the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? Let him curse, because the Most High hath said unto him, Curse David; who shall then say, Wherefore hast thou done so?
- David rolled with mighty men of war, so Abishai was ready to take Shimei's head off his shoulders. But David said to let him curse, for if it was of the Most High, then let him do it. Just as the Most High brings people to our forums and classrooms who bicker and try to bring confusion, it is of the Most High, sometimes to test the patience of those who pray for patience.

**[2 Samuel 16:11-12](/bible/2-samuel/16#v11)**

> <sup>[11](/bible/2-samuel/16#v11)</sup> And David said to Abishai, and to all his servants, Behold, my son, which came forth of my bowels, seeketh my life: how much more now may this Benjamite do it? let him alone, and let him curse; for the Lord hath bidden him.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/2-samuel/16#v12)</sup> It may be that the Lord will look on mine affliction, and that the Lord will requite me good for his cursing this day.

- David said to Abishai and all his servants, Behold, my own son who came forth out of my bowels seeketh my life, how much more now may this Benjamite do it? Let him alone and let him curse, for the Most High hath bidden him. It may be that the Most High will look on his affliction and requite him good for the cursing this day.
- David reasoned that if his own son sought his life, this Benjamite was nothing; the Most High was doing this, so let him curse. It may be the Most High will look on all that was done to David and bless him in front of them, the same as when people try to bring us down and the Most High blesses us before them, which is why this congregation has grown exponentially.

**[2 Samuel 16:13-19](/bible/2-samuel/16#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/2-samuel/16#v13)</sup> And as David and his men went by the way, Shimei went along on the hill’s side over against him, and cursed as he went, and threw stones at him, and cast dust.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/2-samuel/16#v14)</sup> And the king, and all the people that were with him, came weary, and refreshed themselves there.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/2-samuel/16#v15)</sup> And Absalom, and all the people the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/2-samuel/16#v16)</sup> And it came to pass, when Hushai the Archite, David’s friend, was come unto Absalom, that Hushai said unto Absalom, God save the king, God save the king.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/2-samuel/16#v17)</sup> And Absalom said to Hushai, Is this thy kindness to thy friend? why wentest thou not with thy friend?
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/2-samuel/16#v18)</sup> And Hushai said unto Absalom, Nay; but whom the Lord, and this people, and all the men of Israel, choose, his will I be, and with him will I abide.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/2-samuel/16#v19)</sup> And again, whom should I serve? should I not serve in the presence of his son? as I have served in thy father’s presence, so will I be in thy presence.

- David and his men went by the way while Shimei went along the hillside cursing, throwing stones, and casting dust; and they came weary and refreshed themselves. Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him. When Hushai the Archite, David's friend, came to Absalom saying, God save the king, Absalom asked why he went not with his friend, and Hushai answered that he would serve whom the Most High and Israel chose, and would serve in the presence of the son as he served the father.
- Hushai put into action the plan he and David made. Absalom challenged him, asking, Is this thy kindness to thy friend? Why wentest thou not with thy friend? This is a real friend, not a friendish one; a true friend tells you when you are wrong and full of it, not the one who only strokes your head and pats your back like Absalom did to steal the people's hearts.

**[2 Samuel 16:20-23](/bible/2-samuel/16#v20)**

> <sup>[20](/bible/2-samuel/16#v20)</sup> Then said Absalom to Ahithophel, Give counsel among you what we shall do.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/2-samuel/16#v21)</sup> And Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Go in unto thy father’s concubines, which he hath left to keep the house; and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father: then shall the hands of all that are with thee be strong.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/2-samuel/16#v22)</sup> So they spread Absalom a tent upon the top of the house; and Absalom went in unto his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/2-samuel/16#v23)</sup> And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in those days, was as if a man had enquired at the oracle of God: so was all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.

- Absalom asked Ahithophel for counsel, and Ahithophel said, Go in unto thy father's concubines whom he left to keep the house, and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father, and the hands of all with thee shall be strong. So they spread Absalom a tent on the top of the house, and Absalom went in unto his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel. The counsel of Ahithophel was as if a man had inquired at the oracle of God.
- Ahithophel counselled Absalom to lie with the ten concubines David left, in the sight of all Israel, on the roof of the house. This is the exact fulfillment of what the Most High spoke in chapter 12, that David's wives would be taken and one would lie with them in the sight of the sun, and that what David did secretly would be done before all Israel. It was not coincidence or irony; it was prophesied to happen, and none of it would have happened if David had not done what he did. The Most High keeps mercy and forgives, but by no means clears the guilty, so even when we come in and repent, we still must remember the fear of the Most High, for there is but one step between us and death.

  Precepts:
  - **[2 Samuel 12:11-12](/bible/2-samuel/12#v11)**
    > <sup>[11](/bible/2-samuel/12#v11)</sup> Thus saith the Lord, Behold, I will raise up evil against thee out of thine own house, and I will take thy wives before thine eyes, and give them unto thy neighbour, and he shall lie with thy wives in the sight of this sun.
    >
    > <sup>[12](/bible/2-samuel/12#v12)</sup> For thou didst it secretly: but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.

    The Most High would raise up evil out of David's own house and give his wives to his neighbour in the sight of the sun, done before all Israel because David did it secretly.
  - **[Exodus 34:7](/bible/exodus/34#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/exodus/34#v7)</sup> Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children’s children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.

    The Most High keeps mercy and forgives iniquity, but will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children.
  - **[1 Peter 2:20](/bible/1-peter/2#v20)**
    > <sup>[20](/bible/1-peter/2#v20)</sup> For what glory is it, if, when ye be buffeted for your faults, ye shall take it patiently? but if, when ye do well, and suffer for it, ye take it patiently, this is acceptable with God.

    If ye take it patiently when ye do well and suffer for it, this is acceptable with God.
